summaryEn: Episode 47 of "Box of Islam", continuing the presenter's "Islamic fascism" series on Islam, sex and women, argues that the Islamic conception of paradise is an explicitly sexual reward system invented by a desert man, and that this sexualized paradise is functionally tied to jihad. He opens with a clip of a preacher describing the arithmetic of houris, handmaidens and seventy-year sexual encounters in paradise, then argues that this vision originates in the Qur'an itself, that it degrades women by making them sexual objects even in the afterlife, that Islam offers no guarantee of salvation except martyrdom (citing Abu Bakr's fear of God's makr and Q 9:111), and that this combination motivates suicide attackers. He then argues that hadiths about Muhammad's sexual strength of thirty men, the marriage to Safiyya on the night her husband and kin were killed, the absence of a waiting period for captives, and the promise of "the daughters of the yellow ones" at Tabuk all show sex being deployed as a military incentive, that rape of captives functioned both as reward and as a means of turning wombs into an Islamic endowment, and that ISIS's enslavement of Yazidi women replicates the prophetic precedent. He closes by linking this inherited image of women to sexual harassment by Arab migrants in Europe and to Salafi rulings about not sitting on a seat a woman has warmed, and ends with a clip he presents as an example of preacher fabrication about the US Congress.

claims.claimEn: The speaker plays a preacher who claims that every Muslim man in paradise receives at minimum two houris, each houri accompanied by seventy handmaidens, and that both the houri and the handmaiden are sexually lawful to him.
claims.claimAr: يعرض المقدم شيخاً يزعم أن لكل مسلم في الجنة حوريتين على الأقل، مع كل حورية سبعون وصيفة، وأن الحورية والوصيفة كلتيهما حلال له جنسياً.
claims.verificationNote: Identify the preacher and the hadith or exegetical sources behind the claim of two houris per believer, seventy handmaidens per houri, and the sexual lawfulness of handmaidens; check Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and paradise-description literature for these numbers.

claims.claimEn: The speaker plays a preacher who claims the women of paradise are ranked in three or four classes — the worldly wife first, then the houri who is described as a possession of the right hand (mulk al-yamin), then the handmaiden, described the way the immortal youths are described.
claims.claimAr: يعرض المقدم شيخاً يزعم أن نساء الجنة على ثلاث أو أربع مراتب — زوجة الدنيا أولاً، ثم الحورية وهي كملك اليمين، ثم الوصيفة التي توصف كما وُصف الولدان المخلدون.
claims.verificationNote: Check whether classical sources describe houris as mulk al-yamin and rank paradise women in classes, and locate the Qur'anic phrase al-wildan al-mukhalladun (Q 56:17, 76:19) used as the comparison.

claims.claimEn: The speaker plays a preacher who claims a single sexual encounter with a wife in paradise lasts seventy earthly years, after which a second, more beautiful houri calls the believer from a higher level, and this rotation repeats every seventy years indefinitely.
claims.claimAr: يعرض المقدم شيخاً يزعم أن اللقاء الجنسي الواحد بالزوجة في الجنة يمتد سبعين سنة من سنوات الدنيا، ثم تناديه حورية ثانية أجمل من درجة أعلى، ويتكرر هذا التبديل كل سبعين سنة بلا انتهاء.
claims.verificationNote: Trace the seventy-year-encounter motif and the calling houri to its hadith or preaching source; check whether it appears in canonical collections or only in later homiletic literature.

claims.claimEn: The speaker plays a preacher who claims the Qur'anic phrase "and with Us is more" (wa-ladayna mazid) and the verse "no soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for the eyes" both refer to additional houris awaiting the believer.
claims.claimAr: يعرض المقدم شيخاً يزعم أن قوله «ولدينا مزيد» وقوله «فلا تعلم نفس ما أخفي لهم من قرة أعين» يشيران إلى حوريات إضافيات في انتظار المؤمن.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the sexualized picture of paradise found in the hadiths starts in the Qur'an itself, which made the human being's pleasure in paradise a sexual pleasure — meat of birds, grapes, wine and women — rather than liberation from appetite and elevation above the animal side of the human.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن الصورة الجنسية للجنة في الأحاديث بادئة من القرآن نفسه الذي جعل متعة الإنسان في الجنة متعة جنسية — لحم طير وعنب وخمر ونساء — بدل التحرر من النزوات والسمو فوق الجانب الحيواني.

claims.verificationNote: Check Q 33:50 for the wording on cousins and the woman who offers herself, and classical exegesis on its occasion of revelation.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the Qur'anic descriptions of wide-eyed houris and of houris cloistered in pavilions are further evidence that the text imagines God describing sexual rewards, which he presents as implausible for a divine author.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن أوصاف حور العين والحور المقصورات في الخيام دليل إضافي على أن النص يتصور الله يصف مكافآت جنسية، وهو ما يقدمه بوصفه غير معقول عن مؤلف إلهي.
claims.verificationNote: Check Q 55:72 (hur maqsurat fi al-khiyam) and the hur 'in verses, and the classical exegesis of these descriptions.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims sex is the shortest route by which a young Muslim obtains all this bliss and escapes hellfire, since every other path is uncertain.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن هذا هو أقصر الطرق للشاب المسلم لينال كل هذا النعيم وينجو من عذاب النار، لأن أي طريق آخر غير مضمون.
claims.verificationNote: Inference from the earlier salvation and martyrdom claims; verify those rather than this restatement.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims some young men carrying out suicide operations wrap their penis in aluminium foil so that it remains intact for the houris who will receive them upon direct transfer to paradise without reckoning.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن بعض الشباب في العمليات الانتحارية يغلفون القضيب بورق ألمونيوم ليبقى سليماً للحوريات، مع الانتقال المباشر إلى الجنة بدون حساب.
claims.verificationNote: Check forensic and journalistic reporting on suicide bombers wrapping genitals before attacks, and whether the practice is documented rather than anecdotal.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the idea of sex in Islam has an important instrumental use: Muhammad was concerned to keep Muslims — or the fighters — under his control and motivated.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن فكرة الجنس في الإسلام لها توظيف مهم: محمد كان يهمه أن يبقى المسلمون أو المقاتلون تحت سيطرته ومتحفزين.
claims.verificationNote: Assess against sirah and maghazi accounts whether sexual reward is used as an instrument of command and motivation.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims there are many hadiths about the prophet's sexual power, stating he had the strength of thirty men, and asks what instrument in Mecca or Medina could have measured such a figure precisely — why thirty and not thirty-seven or thirty-eight — presenting the precision as a sign of fabrication.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن هناك أحاديث كثيرة عن القوة الجنسية للرسول تقول إن له قوة ثلاثين رجلاً، ويسأل بأي جهاز في مكة أو المدينة قيس هذا الرقم بدقة — لماذا ثلاثون لا سبعة وثلاثون ولا ثمانية وثلاثون — مقدماً هذه الدقة دليل اختلاق.
claims.verificationNote: Locate the hadiths on the prophet's sexual strength being that of thirty (or forty) men, e.g. in Bukhari and Musnad Ahmad, and check the numbers actually stated.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the hadiths on the prophet's sexual strength have a jihadist function: they establish that the Muslim man is sexually powerful, meaning a penetrator of the enemy's wombs.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن أحاديث القوة الجنسية للنبي لها وظيفة جهادية: تقرر أن الرجل المسلم قوي جنسياً، أي مقتحم لأرحام الأعداء.
claims.verificationNote: Interpretive inference; check whether early sources link the prophet's sexual strength to military virility rhetoric.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims rape in the Islamic wars was not mere pleasure but had a first function of rewarding Muslim soldiers, whose motives were not always doctrinal, with material spoils and captive women, thereby encouraging more soldiers to join the campaigns.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن الاغتصاب في الحروب الإسلامية لم يكن مجرد متعة بل وظيفته الأولى مكافأة الجنود المسلمين، الذين لم تكن دوافعهم دائماً عقائدية، بالغنائم المادية والسبايا، مما يشجع جنوداً أكثر على المشاركة.
claims.verificationNote: Check maghazi and futuh literature on the distribution of captives as part of spoils and whether sources present this as a recruitment incentive.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the description of Muhammad as a mercy to the worlds does not extend to captives or to children taken as slaves, because in the Qur'an "the worlds" and the address "O mankind" mean Muslims only — non-Muslims such as the Yazidi women are not included among "the worlds" or among humans.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن وصف محمد بأنه رحمة للعالمين لا يشمل السبايا ولا الأطفال المأخوذين عبيداً، لأن «العالمين» و«يا أيها الناس» في القرآن تعني المسلمين وحدهم — وغير المسلمين كاليزيديات ليسوا من العالمين ولا من البشر.
claims.verificationNote: Check Q 21:107 (rahmatan lil-'alamin) and the scope of the ya ayyuha al-nas address in classical exegesis against the speaker's restriction to Muslims.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims a second function of wartime rape: the wife of the unbeliever or People of the Book, in a land raided or conquered under the banner of Islam, has until then borne unbelievers, so when the Muslim man storms and rapes her he "opens her womb with the word of God", after which that womb becomes an Islamic endowment (waqf) bearing Muslim children — making rape a virtue.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن للاغتصاب الحربي وظيفة ثانية: زوجة الكافر أو الكتابي في بلد يُغار عليه أو يُفتح تحت راية الإسلام كانت تلد كفاراً، فإذا اقتحمها الرجل المسلم واغتصبها «افتتح رحمها بكلمة الله»، فيصير هذا الرحم وقفاً إسلامياً ينجب أطفالاً مسلمين، فيصير الاغتصاب فضيلة.
claims.verificationNote: Check whether any classical juristic or homiletic source articulates this womb-conversion rationale, and whether the children of captive women were held to follow the father's religion.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims that when ISIS raped Yazidi women and Muslims replied that these are savages with no connection to Islam and that Islam is innocent of them, they were overlooking that this is exactly the scenario the prophet enacted with Safiyya.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن المسلمين حين قالوا عن اغتصاب داعش لليزيديات إن هؤلاء متوحشون لا علاقة لهم بالإسلام وإن الإسلام بريء منهم، أغفلوا أن هذا هو سيناريو النبي مع صفية بعينه.
claims.verificationNote: Compare the sirah accounts of Safiyya bint Huyayy at Khaybar with documented ISIS practice regarding Yazidi captives to test the claimed identity of the scenarios.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the prophet had intercourse with Safiyya on the very night her husband was killed — her father having been killed a year earlier, or in another version her husband and her father killed together — and that a man whose forces erased her tribe within a day and a night took her as a war captive without waiting for her husband's blood to cool.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن النبي وطئ صفية في نفس الليلة التي قُتل فيها زوجها — وقد قُتل أبوها قبلها بسنة، أو في رواية قُتل زوجها وأبوها معاً — وأن رجلاً محا قبيلتها من الوجود في يوم وليلة أخذها سبية ولم ينتظر حتى يبرد دم زوجها.
claims.verificationNote: Check Bukhari, Muslim, Ibn Ishaq and Waqidi on the timing of Safiyya's consummation relative to the killing of Kinana b. al-Rabi' and of Huyayy b. Akhtab.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the traditional apologetic that God opened Safiyya's heart to Islam and that she was captivated by Islam is implausible, since it would require her to have been dreaming of a knight from Arabia who would wipe out her tribe, take her as a war captive and sleep with her the same night.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن الاعتذار التقليدي بأن الله شرح صدر صفية للإسلام وأنها كانت منبهرة بالإسلام غير معقول، إذ يقتضي أنها كانت تحلم بفارس مغوار من الجزيرة العربية يمحو قبيلتها ويأخذها سبية حرب وينامها في الليلة نفسها.
claims.verificationNote: Compare the sirah reports on Safiyya's stated attitude toward Islam with the circumstances of her capture recorded in the same sources.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims that although Islam prescribes a waiting period ('idda) that would establish whether a woman is pregnant, the 'idda does not apply to female captives — whether married or not, the moment her tribe or land falls under Islamic rule she has no husband, no children of her own, her children become the captor's slaves, and her body and all of her become his property to dispose of as he wishes.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أنه رغم أن الإسلام شرع العدة التي تبين حمل المرأة، فإن العدة لا تسري على السبية — متزوجة أو غير متزوجة، ففي لحظة سقوط قبيلتها أو أرضها تحت الحكم الإسلامي لا زوج لها ولا أطفال، بل يصير أطفالها عبيداً للسابي، وجسمها وكلها ملكه يتصرف فيها كيف يشاء.
claims.verificationNote: Check the fiqh rules on istibra' for captives versus 'idda for free women, and the hadiths on intercourse with captives (e.g. the Awtas reports) against this characterization.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims that if Islam liberated women it liberated only Muslim women and not the women of all the worlds, and that it failed to free women from captivity, enslavement and rape because captivity had an instrumental function in encouraging and controlling the armies.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن الإسلام إن كان حرر المرأة فقد حرر المسلمة وحدها لا نساء العالمين، وأنه لم يحرر النساء من الأسر والسبي والاغتصاب لأن للسبي وظيفة في تشجيع الجحافل والسيطرة عليها.
claims.verificationNote: Assess the apologetic claim that Islam liberated women against the legal status of captive and enslaved women in the same sources.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims Muhammad, when raiding the Byzantines, would motivate his fighters with "the daughters of the yellow ones" (banat al-asfar), and cites a hadith urging "raid Tabuk and you will attain the daughters of the yellow ones".
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن محمداً كان يشجع محاربيه ببنات الأصفر كلما غزا الروم، ويستشهد بحديث «اغزوا تبوك تنالوا بنات الأصفر».
claims.verificationNote: Locate the report on Tabuk and banat al-asfar (reported in tafsir of Q 9 and in sirah/maghazi literature) and check its exact wording and chains.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the daughters of the Byzantines had a higher slave value than other concubines.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن بنات الأصفر كان لهن قيمة كعبيد أغلى من قيمة الجواري الأخريات.
claims.verificationNote: Check historical slave-market price data for Byzantine or fair-skinned captives relative to other categories in early Islamic sources.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims ISIS applied the same logic today, citing a video in which a blue-eyed girl is priced higher as a slave.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن داعش طبقت المنطق نفسه اليوم، مستشهداً بفيديو يقول إن البنت زرقاء العينين أغلى كعابدة.
claims.verificationNote: Locate the ISIS video or documented slave price list on the valuation of blue-eyed captives.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims that, connecting to the previous episode on sexual harassment, an Arab young man who migrates to Europe sees the local woman either as the porn actress he watched or as one of the war captives of Islam he reads about in history, and concludes that having entered her land he is entitled to have her beneath him.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم، رابطاً بالحلقة السابقة عن التحرش الجنسي، أن الشاب العربي المهاجر إلى أوروبا يرى المرأة هناك إما ممثلة البورنو التي كان يشاهدها وإما سبية من سبايا الإسلام التي يقرأ عنها في التاريخ، ويستنتج أنه ما دام اقتحم أرضها فمن حقه أن تكون تحته.
claims.verificationNote: Sociological inference; check whether it rests on any cited data beyond the speaker's reasoning from the captivity precedent.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims that whether the individual is religious or not is not the decisive factor: he is saturated in this civilization and culture, which has become part of his composition, so it shapes his mental image of woman as nothing but a sexual dimension — obtained either by a marriage contract or by taking her as a war captive with no contract and no obligations, under his control.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن كون الشخص متديناً أو غير متدين ليس هو العامل الحاسم: فهو متشبع بهذه الحضارة والثقافة التي صارت جزءاً من تركيبته، فتشكل صورته الذهنية عن المرأة بحيث لا يرى فيها إلا الجانب الجنسي — يُنال إما بعقد نكاح وإما بأخذها سبية حرب بلا عقد ولا التزامات تحت سيطرته.
claims.verificationNote: Cultural inference; verify the underlying legal categories of nikah and concubinage it relies on rather than the sociological conclusion.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims Islam's view of sex is unnatural and was not framed with any anticipation of how humanity would develop, whereas contemporary societies are built on parity between men and women.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن نظرة الإسلام للجنس غير طبيعية ولم توضع باستشراف لتطور البشرية، بينما المجتمعات المعاصرة قائمة على الندية بين الرجل والمرأة.
claims.verificationNote: Evaluative comparison; no source locator to verify beyond the legal rules already recorded.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims Salafis in Egypt taught that a man may not shake a woman's hand and may not even sit on a chair a woman has just vacated because her body's warmth remains on it, and presents this as contempt for human dignity that sees only an animal in the person — an animal that would not itself be aroused by a warm chair.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن السلفيين في مصر كانوا يقولون إن الرجل ممنوع من مصافحة المرأة، بل وممنوع من الجلوس على الكرسي الذي قامت عنه لأن دفء جسدها ما زال عليه، ويقدم ذلك احتقاراً لأدمية الإنسان لا يرى فيه إلا حيواناً — والحيوان نفسه لا يثار من كرسي دافئ.
claims.verificationNote: Locate the Egyptian Salafi fatwas prohibiting handshaking and sitting on a seat warmed by a woman, and identify the scholars who issued them.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the rulings rest on threats in the tradition that a man who gives his hand to a woman will be sunk into the earth seventy cubits, or struck with a spike of iron or of fire, and that such a picture automatically produces a pathological way of dealing with women.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن هذه الأحكام تستند إلى وعيد في التراث بأن من أعطى يده لامرأة يُخسف به في الأرض سبعين ذراعاً أو يُضرب بمخيط من حديد أو من نار، وأن هذه الصورة تجعل الإنسان تلقائياً يتعامل مع المرأة بأسلوب مرضي.
claims.verificationNote: Trace the hadith about a head being pierced with an iron needle rather than touching a woman (attributed to Tabarani) and any report about sinking seventy cubits, and check their wording and grading.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims violence, sexual harassment and the social disintegration visible in the Arab world are all interconnected phenomena and represent the beginnings of collapse.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن العنف والتحرش الجنسي وانحلال المجتمعات الذي نراه في العالم العربي ظواهر مترابطة وأنها بدايات السقوط.
claims.verificationNote: Broad sociological conclusion with no source locator; verify only the specific rulings and reports it builds on.

claims.claimEn: The speaker claims the rot eating into Islamic societies is caused by moral hypocrisy, and that despite this Muslims still say the West learns from them and copies their experience.
claims.claimAr: يزعم المقدم أن السوس الذي بدأ ينخر المجتمعات الإسلامية سببه النفاق الأخلاقي، وأن المسلمين مع ذلك يقولون إن الغرب يتعلم منهم وينقل تجاربهم.
claims.verificationNote: Evaluative claim about contemporary societies; no primary source to check.

claims.claimEn: The speaker plays a preacher who claims that when the number of street children born of fornication grew in America, the US Congress convened thinkers and inventors for three days of brainstorming and their solution was to separate young men from young women — and that the capitalists likewise concluded that Islamic banks must be established — which the speaker presents without comment as an example of preacher fabrication about the West.
claims.claimAr: يعرض المقدم شيخاً يزعم أن الكونغرس الأمريكي، لما كثر أبناء الزنا وأبناء الشوارع في أمريكا، جمع المفكرين والمخترعين ثلاثة أيام من العصف الذهني فكان الحل هو عزل الشباب عن الفتيات، وأن الرأسماليين كذلك وجدوا الحل في إنشاء بنوك إسلامية، ويقدم المقدم ذلك بلا تعليق مثالاً على اختلاق الدعاة عن الغرب.
claims.verificationNote: Identify the preacher in the closing clip and check whether any US Congressional proceeding on street children or Islamic banking of the kind described ever occurred.

topicProposals.descriptionEn: Claims about the houris, handmaidens and sensual rewards described for paradise in the Qur'an and hadith, their arithmetic and elaboration in preaching, the asymmetry between men's and women's rewards, and readings of these descriptions as evidence of a human, male author.
topicProposals.descriptionAr: دعاوى عن الحور والوصائف والمكافآت الحسية الموصوفة للجنة في القرآن والحديث، وحسابها وتوسعها في الخطاب الوعظي، واختلال المكافأة بين الرجل والمرأة، وقراءة هذه الأوصاف دليلاً على مؤلف بشري ذكر.
topicProposals.rationale: The episode returns repeatedly to the description of paradise as a sexual reward system — houri counts, seventy-year encounters, mulk al-yamin status of houris, the absence of any equivalent reward for women. This is a durable subject other videos in this series and in the wider polemical literature also address, and it currently has no home: hadith-ethical-controversies covers conduct and rulings, not eschatological description, and quran-lexical-and-interpretive-questions covers only terminology.

topicProposals.descriptionEn: Claims that fighting in Islam is sustained by promised rewards — guaranteed paradise for the martyr, spoils, captive women — and that these promises functioned as recruitment, motivation and control of fighters, from the maghazi campaigns to modern militant movements.
topicProposals.descriptionAr: دعاوى بأن القتال في الإسلام قائم على مكافآت موعودة — الجنة المضمونة للشهيد والغنائم والسبايا — وأن هذه الوعود عملت أداة تجنيد وتحفيز وسيطرة على المقاتلين، من المغازي إلى الحركات المسلحة الحديثة.
topicProposals.rationale: The episode's central thesis is that sexual and eschatological reward is functionally wired to jihad — Q 9:111, the Tabuk banat al-asfar report, the distribution of captives, suicide operations. sirah-conflict-and-political-conduct covers the events themselves but not the reward-and-motivation mechanism, which recurs across this series and across the wider corpus of critical material.

topicProposals.titleEn: Da'wah rhetoric and fabricated claims about the West
topicProposals.titleAr: خطاب الدعاة والدعاوى المختلقة عن الغرب
topicProposals.descriptionEn: Claims about assertions made by modern preachers that are presented as history or news — invented Western institutional decisions, conversions, and scientific endorsements — and the rhetorical function these fabrications serve in contemporary da'wah.
topicProposals.descriptionAr: دعاوى عن مزاعم يطلقها الدعاة المعاصرون بوصفها تاريخاً أو خبراً — قرارات مؤسسية غربية مختلقة وإسلام مشاهير وشهادات علمية — والوظيفة الخطابية التي تؤديها هذه الاختلاقات في الدعوة المعاصرة.
topicProposals.rationale: The closing clip about the US Congress and Islamic banks is a fabricated claim about the West used homiletically, a recurring genre in this series. scientific-miracles-apologetics-movement covers only the i'jaz 'ilmi strand of this rhetoric; the broader pattern of invented Western episodes has no home in the taxonomy.
